work: Enarratio in Epistolam B. Pauli ad Hebræos
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

6.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI SEXTI : QUAPROPTER INTERMITTENTES, ETC.
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: Wherefore, leaving, etc.

paras.t: Posita increpatione Hebræorum, subjungitur blanda exhortatio eorumdem. Quapropter, videlicet quoniam perfectorum est solidus cibus, intermittentes inchoationis Christi sermonem, id est prima atque communia christianæ doctrinæ principia, ut sunt articuli fidei, ad perfectionem, id est ad veram sapientiam et sanctam conversationem, feramur, id est moveamur, Deo per gratiam nos intus excitante, et proximo adjuvante, vel anima se ipsam hortante. Consequenter ostendit Apostolus quæ sunt quæ velit jam prætermittere, eo quod spectent ad inchoationem sermonis Christi, tanquam fidei rudimenta quibus novelli in fide instrui habent. Sunt autem sex, sicut patebit. Non rursum jacientes fundamentum pœnitentiæ, id est non iterum tractantes de sacramento Pœnitentiæ, quæ est primum fundamentum quantum ad peccatores adultos baptizatos, gratiam adipisci conantes : quæ pœnitentia est ab operibus mortuis, id est recessus ac dolor de peccatis, quæ interficiunt animam. Nec rursus jacientes fundamentum fidei ad Deum, id est, non iterum de ipsa fide, quæ est fundamentum virtutum, loquentes, videlicet de nuda ac simplici fide. Infra tamen fit sermo prolixus de fide idonea atque perfecta.
paras.en: Having set down his rebuke of the Hebrews, he adds a gentle exhortation to them. [[6:1|Wherefore|Quapropter]], namely, since strong meat is for the perfect, [[6:1|leaving the word of the beginning of Christ|intermittentes inchoationis Christi sermonem]], that is, the first and common principles of Christian doctrine, such as the articles of faith, to perfection [Denis reads *ad perfectionem* where the Vulgate has *ad perfectiora*], that is, to true wisdom and holy conversation, [[6:1|let us go on|feramur]], that is, let us be moved, God stirring us inwardly by grace, and our neighbour helping, or the soul exhorting itself. Next the Apostle shows what the things are which he now wishes to pass over, because they belong to the beginning of the word of Christ, as the rudiments of faith in which the newly converted are to be instructed. And they are six, as will appear. [[6:1|not laying again the foundation of penance|Non rursum jacientes fundamentum pœnitentiæ]], that is, not treating again of the sacrament of Penance, which is the first foundation for adult baptized sinners striving to obtain grace: which penance is [[6:1|from dead works|ab operibus mortuis]], that is, a withdrawal from and sorrow for sins, which kill the soul. Nor again laying the foundation [[6:1|of faith towards God|fidei ad Deum]], that is, not speaking again of faith itself, which is the foundation of the virtues, namely of bare and simple faith. Below, however, a lengthy discourse is made of fitting and perfect faith.

paras.t: Baptismatum doctrinæ, id est non denuo determinantes de Baptismo christianæ legis. Dicit autem pluraliter, Baptismatum, propter triplex Baptisma, videlicet fluminis, flaminis et sanguinis. Impositionis quoque manuum, id est, non iterum tractantes de sacramento Confirmationis, in quo datur Spiritus Sanctus ac robur animæ per impositionem manuum. Ac resurrectionis mortuorum, id est, non de generali mortuorum resurrectione rursus agentes. Et judicii æterni, id est, non de finali judicio denuo pertractantes : quod ideo appellatur æternum, quia effectus sententiæ Judicis, scilicet merces reddenda, æternaliter durat. Et hoc faciemus, id est, prædicto modo procedemus, faciliora prætermittendo et ad perfectionem tendendo, si quidem permiserit Deus, id est, si tempus vivendi, gratiamque adimplendi præstiterit.
paras.en: [[6:2|Of the doctrine of baptisms|Baptismatum doctrinæ]], that is, not determining anew concerning the Baptism of the Christian law. He says *baptisms* in the plural because of the threefold Baptism, namely of water, of the Spirit and of blood [Latin *fluminis, flaminis et sanguinis*, a jingle: of the stream, of the breath, of blood]. [[6:2|and imposition of hands|Impositionis quoque manuum]], that is, not treating again of the sacrament of Confirmation, in which the Holy Ghost and strength of soul are given by the imposition of hands. [[6:2|and of the resurrection of the dead|Ac resurrectionis mortuorum]], that is, not dealing again with the general resurrection of the dead. [[6:2|and of eternal judgment|Et judicii æterni]], that is, not treating anew of the final judgment, which is called eternal because the effect of the Judge's sentence, namely the reward to be rendered, endures eternally. [[6:3|And this will we do|Et hoc faciemus]], that is, we shall proceed in the said manner, passing over the easier things and tending to perfection, [[6:3|if God permit|si quidem permiserit Deus]], that is, if He grant time to live and grace to fulfil it.

paras.t: Impossibile est enim, eos, etc. Hoc tribus modis exponitur. Primo sic : Ad perfectionem feramur, nec opinemur nos posse per Baptismum sæpius emundari. Impossibile est enim, eos qui semel sunt illuminati, id est, fidem et gratiam primo receperunt in fonte Baptismatis, et gustaverunt donum cœleste, id est, divinæ pietatis effectum, videlicet peccatorum remissionem et consolationem internam, experti sunt, et participes facti sunt Spiritus Sancti, id est, septem dona Spiritus Sancti sortiti sunt : quæ omnia simul cum gratia gratum faciente infunduntur, et simul cum ea habentur atque perduntur ; gustaverunt nihilo minus bonum Dei verbum, id est, Christi dulcedinem secundum ejus divinitatem contemplando ac diligendo senserunt : de quo verbo Pater testatur, Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum ; vel, Bonum Dei verbum, id est evangelicæ doctrinæ sermonem, ita ut dicere valeant : Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua ! Illud quoque Jeremiæ : Factus est sermo Domini in corde meo quasi ignis exæstuans, claususque in ossibus meis ; et defeci, ferre non sustinens ; virtutesque sæculi venturi, id est, cœlestes perfectiones, seu animæ et corporis dotes in patria habendas jam gustaverunt per spem seu aliquam prælibationem ac inchoationem : et prolapsi sunt, id est, post tanta beneficia in vitia corruerunt : renovari rursus, id est spiritualiter regenerari, ad pœnitentiam, id est ad gratiam pœnitendi, videlicet ut gratiam reparent per Baptismum, rursum crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium Dei, id est, isti qui per Baptismi iterationem resurgere putant a culpis, iterum, quantum in ipsis est, et ad propriam damnationem, crucifigunt Christum, et ostentui habentes, id est, eum irrident. Nam et crucifixoribus et irrisoribus Christi consimiles sunt. Quum enim in Baptismo configurentur Christo passo atque sepulto (juxta quod dictum est ad Romanos : Quicumque baptizati sumus in Christo Jesu, in morte ipsius baptizati sumus ; consepulti enim sumus cum illo per Baptismum, etc.), dum ergo asserunt Baptismum iterari posse, passionem quoque ipsius iterabilem fore protestari videntur.
paras.en: [[6:4|For it is impossible for those|Impossibile est enim, eos]], etc. This is expounded in three ways. First thus: Let us go on to perfection, and let us not suppose that we can be cleansed more than once by Baptism. [[6:4|For it is impossible for those who were once illuminated|Impossibile est enim, eos qui semel sunt illuminati]], that is, who first received faith and grace in the font of Baptism, [[6:4|have tasted also the heavenly gift|et gustaverunt donum cœleste]], that is, have experienced the effect of divine mercy, namely the remission of sins and inward consolation, [[6:4|and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost|et participes facti sunt Spiritus Sancti]], that is, have received the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]][[Is 11:3||]], all of which are infused together with sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God], and are had and lost together with it; [[6:5|Have moreover tasted the good word of God|gustaverunt nihilo minus bonum Dei verbum]], that is, have felt the sweetness of Christ according to His divinity by contemplating and loving Him: of which Word the Father testifies, [[Ps 44:2|My heart hath uttered a good word|Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum]]; or, the good word of God, that is, the discourse of the gospel teaching, so that they can say: [[Ps 118:103|How sweet are thy words to my palate!|Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua]]! And that of Jeremias: [[Jer 20:9|and there came in my heart as a burning fire, shut up in my bones, and I was wearied, not being able to bear it|Factus est sermo Domini in corde meo quasi ignis exæstuans, claususque in ossibus meis ; et defeci, ferre non sustinens]]; [[6:5|and the powers of the world to come|virtutesque sæculi venturi]], that is, have already tasted, by hope or some foretaste and beginning, the heavenly perfections, or the endowments of soul and body to be had in the fatherland: [[6:6|And are fallen away|et prolapsi sunt]], that is, after such great benefits have fallen headlong into vices: [[6:6|to be renewed again|renovari rursus]], that is, to be spiritually regenerated, [[6:6|to penance|ad pœnitentiam]], that is, to the grace of repenting, namely so as to recover grace by Baptism, [[6:6|crucifying again to themselves the Son of God|rursum crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium Dei]], that is, those who think to rise from their sins by repeating Baptism crucify Christ again, as far as in them lies, and to their own damnation, [[6:6|and making him a mockery|et ostentui habentes]], that is, they mock Him. For they are like those who crucified and mocked Christ. Since in Baptism they are conformed to Christ who suffered and was buried (according to what is said to the Romans: [[Rom 6:3|all we who are baptized in Christ Jesus are baptized in his death?|Quicumque baptizati sumus in Christo Jesu, in morte ipsius baptizati sumus]]; [[Rom 6:4|For we are buried together with him by baptism into death|consepulti enim sumus cum illo per Baptismum]], etc.), when therefore they assert that Baptism can be repeated, they seem to declare that His passion too can be repeated.

paras.t: Secundo, exponitur de quocumque recidivante, qui post prædicta beneficia in magna peccata prolabitur, et in iis quodammodo habituatur. Non enim homo prædictas gratias experitur, nisi sit valde perfectus. Talis vero non subito evacuatur, sed paulatim, donec penitus obtenebretur. Tales ergo ad pœnitentiam renovari, id est iterum emendari et pœnitere, impossibile est, id est difficile. Secundum quem modum peccata in Spiritum Sanctum dicuntur irremissibilia. Et Christus Judæis dixit : Quomodo potestis loqui bona, quum sitis mali? Sic enim apud Prophetam legitur : Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, et vos poteritis bene facere. Hujusmodi quoque iterum crucifigunt sibi Filium Dei, quoniam quantum in ipsis est, causam suæ crucifixionis reiterant. — Tertio, exponitur pro statu futuri sæculi, ut sit sensus, quod prædicti renovari non possunt ad pœnitentiam post hanc vitam, secundum quod scriptum est : Venit nox quando nemo potest operari.
paras.en: Secondly, it is expounded of any backslider who, after the said benefits, falls into great sins and becomes in a manner habituated to them. For a man does not experience the said graces unless he is very perfect. Such a one is not emptied out suddenly, but little by little, until he is wholly darkened. For such, then, to be renewed to penance, that is, to amend and repent again, is *impossible*, that is, difficult. In this sense sins against the Holy Ghost are said to be unforgivable. And Christ said to the Jews: [[Matt 12:34|how can you speak good things, whereas you are evil?|Quomodo potestis loqui bona, quum sitis mali]]? For so we read in the Prophet: [[Jer 13:23|If the Ethiopian can change his skin|Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam]], you also may do well. Such men too crucify again to themselves the Son of God, since, as far as in them lies, they repeat the cause of His crucifixion. — Thirdly, it is expounded of the state of the world to come, so that the sense is that the said persons cannot be renewed to penance after this life, according to what is written: [[John 9:4|the night cometh, when no man can work|Venit nox quando nemo potest operari]].

paras.t: Primus autem intellectus convenientior est. Apostolus enim loquitur Hebræis, amputans eis occasionem errandi circa Baptismum, videlicet ne sic arbitrarentur repeti posse Baptismatis sacramentum, quemadmodum ablutiones et baptismata legis Moysis iterabantur.
paras.en: The first interpretation, however, is the more fitting. For the Apostle is speaking to Hebrews, cutting off from them occasion of error about Baptism, namely lest they should think the sacrament of Baptism could be repeated in the way the washings and baptisms of the law of Moses were repeated.

paras.t: Denique, ex præinductis verbis Apostoli Novatius, Romanæ Ecclesiæ diaconus, sumpsit occasionem hæreticæ impietatis, affirmans sacramentum Pœnitentiæ iterari non posse. Ad cujus erroris confirmationem aliqui adduxerunt quod scriptum est in Job : Ecce hæc tribus vicibus operatur Deus per singulos. Et in libro Regum : Si peccaverit vir in virum, placari ei potest Deus ; si autem in Deum peccaverit, quis exorabit pro eo? Et multa similia in Scripturis habentur, ut quum ait Joannes : Est peccatum ad mortem ; non dico ut pro illo quis oret. Quæ omnia prudenti indigent intellectu, ne verba vitæ et veritatis fiant pabula mortis et falsitatis.
paras.en: Finally, from the aforesaid words of the Apostle Novatius, a deacon of the Roman Church, took occasion for his heretical impiety, affirming that the sacrament of Penance cannot be repeated. In confirmation of this error some adduced what is written in Job: [[Job 33:29|Behold, all these things God worketh three times within every one|Ecce hæc tribus vicibus operatur Deus per singulos]] [Denis's Latin reads literally “three times”]. And in the book of Kings: [[1 Kings 2:25|If one man shall sin against another, God may be appeased in his behalf: but if a man shall sin against the Lord, who shall pray for him?|Si peccaverit vir in virum, placari ei potest Deus ; si autem in Deum peccaverit, quis exorabit pro eo?]]? And many similar things are found in the Scriptures, as when John says: [[1 John 5:16|There is a sin unto death. For that I say not that|Est peccatum ad mortem ; non dico ut pro illo quis oret]]. All of which need prudent understanding, lest the words of life and truth become the food of death and falsehood.

paras.t: Præterea, quod prædicto modo recidivantes, vel rebaptizari volentes, non renoventur ad pœnitentiam, secundum expositiones prætactas, ostendit per simile. Terra enim sæpe venientem super se bibens imbrem, id est, humorem seu pluviam sibi desuper incidentem consumens, et generans herbam opportunam, id est fructum convenientem, illis a quibus colitur mediate et immediate, id est agricolis, seu possessoribus qui eam faciunt arari et exerceri ; accipit benedictionem a Deo, id est, Deo eam fecundante, a suis cultoribus commendatur tanquam fructifera; vel, Accipit benedictionem, id est fecunditatem a Deo, tanquam a prima principalique causa. Proferens autem spinas et tribulos, id est infructuosa exsistens, reproba est et maledicto proxima, id est, reprobatur et tanquam sterilis maledicitur; cujus consummatio, id est fructificatio, scilicet spinarum ac tribulorum productio, erit in combustionem, id est, igni tradetur. — Spiritualiter terra ista est homo, cujus anima accipit imbrem super se venientem, id est cœlestis gratiæ vel sapientiæ salutaris profluvium. Quum autem producit herbam opportunam, id est opera virtuosa, convenientia illis a quibus colitur, id est angelis custodibus et prælatis ac prædicatoribus, accipit benedictionem, id est gratiæ incrementum, a Deo. Habenti enim dabitur, et abundabit. Proferens autem spinas et tribulos, id est passiones acutas et opera prava, reproba est : cujus consummatio, id est finis, erit in combustionem ignis æterni, prout Salvator ait : Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et colligent eum, et in ignem mittent.
paras.en: Further, he shows by a likeness that those who relapse in the said way, or wish to be rebaptized, are not renewed to penance, according to the expositions given above. [[6:7|For the earth, that drinketh in the rain which cometh often upon it|Terra enim sæpe venientem super se bibens imbrem]], that is, consuming the moisture or rain falling on it from above, [[6:7|and bringeth forth herbs meet|et generans herbam opportunam]], that is, fitting fruit, [[6:7|for them by whom it is tilled|illis a quibus colitur]] mediately and immediately, that is, for the husbandmen, or the owners who have it ploughed and worked; [[6:7|receiveth blessing from God|accipit benedictionem a Deo]], that is, God making it fruitful, it is praised by its tillers as fruitful; or, *receiveth blessing*, that is, fruitfulness from God, as from the first and principal cause. [[6:8|But that which bringeth forth thorns and briers|Proferens autem spinas et tribulos]], that is, being unfruitful, [[6:8|is reprobate and very near unto a curse|reproba est et maledicto proxima]], that is, it is rejected and cursed as barren; [[6:8|whose end|cujus consummatio]], that is, its fruiting, namely the production of thorns and briers, [[6:8|is to be burnt|in combustionem]], that is, it will be given to the fire. — Spiritually this earth is man, whose soul receives the rain coming upon it, that is, the outpouring of heavenly grace or saving wisdom. And when it brings forth fit herbs, that is, virtuous works, fitting for those by whom it is tilled, that is, the guardian angels and prelates and preachers, it receives blessing, that is, increase of grace, from God. For [[Matt 25:29|to every one that hath shall be given, and he shall abound|Habenti enim dabitur, et abundabit]]. But bringing forth thorns and briers, that is, sharp passions and wicked works, it is reprobate: whose end will be the burning of eternal fire, as the Saviour says: [[John 15:6|If any one abide not in me, he shall be cast forth as a branch and shall wither: and they shall gather him up and cast him into the fire|Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et colligent eum, et in ignem mittent]].

paras.t: Sed ne propter præinductæ increpationis rigorem exasperarentur, vel pusillanimes fierent, consequenter adjungit blandam consolationem. Confidimus autem de vobis, dilectissimi, meliora et viciniora saluti, id est, perfectiora opera et beatitudinis magis meritoria, vobis inesse speramus, quam superius insinuasse videmur, vel quam sint spinæ ac tribuli quæ suffocant verbum Dei ; tametsi ita loquimur, id est, quamvis tam dure vos increpavimus. Et rationabiliter ita confidimus : Non enim injustus est Deus, cujus virtus justitiæ initium est, ut obliviscatur operis vestri, id est, per modum obliviscentis se habeat, non attendendo nec remunerando vestra opera bona, et dilectionis Dei ac proximi, quam intus latentem, ostendistis foris per actus caritativos (nam exhibitio operis, probatio est caritatis : ideo dicit quoque Salvator, Si quis diligit me, sermones meos servabit), in nomine ipsius, id est propter amorem Dei et gloriam ejus ; quia ministrastis, id est, necessaria vitæ præbuistis et obsequia congrua impendistis, sanctis, id est fide et opere christianis, et ministratis eis, perseverando in opere inchoato : sicut et ad Galatas jam dictum est : Per caritatem servite invicem.
paras.en: But lest they be embittered or grow faint-hearted because of the severity of the foregoing rebuke, he next adds a gentle consolation. [[6:9|But, my dearly beloved, we trust better things of you, and nearer to salvation|Confidimus autem de vobis, dilectissimi, meliora et viciniora saluti]], that is, we hope that there are in you works more perfect and more meritorious of beatitude than we seemed to hint above, or than the thorns and briers which choke the word of God[[Luke 8:7||]][[Luke 8:14||]] [the margin prints Luc. xiii, 7, 14; the parable of the sower is Luke 8:7, 14]; [[6:9|though we speak thus|tametsi ita loquimur]], that is, although we have rebuked you so harshly. And with reason we so trust: [[6:10|For God is not unjust|Non enim injustus est Deus]], whose power is the beginning of justice[[Wis 12:16||]], [[6:10|that he should forget your work|ut obliviscatur operis vestri]], that is, that He should behave as one forgetting, not heeding nor rewarding your good works, [[6:10|and the love|et dilectionis]] of God and neighbour, [[6:10|which you have shewn|quam intus latentem, ostendistis]] outwardly by acts of charity, it being hidden within (for the showing of the work is the proof of charity: hence the Saviour also says, [[John 14:23|If any one love me, he will keep my word|Si quis diligit me, sermones meos servabit]]), [[6:10|in his name|in nomine ipsius]], that is, for the love of God and His glory; [[6:10|you who have ministered|quia ministrastis]], that is, have provided the necessaries of life and rendered fitting services, [[6:10|to the saints|sanctis]], that is, to those who are Christians in faith and deed, [[6:10|and do minister|et ministratis]] to them, persevering in the work begun: as was already said to the Galatians: [[Gal 5:13|by charity of the spirit serve one another|Per caritatem servite invicem]].

paras.t: Cupimus autem, zelo vestræ salutis accensi, unumquemque vestrum eamdem ostentare sollicitudinem, id est præmemoratam sollicitam ministrationem frequenter ostendere, ad expletionem spei, id est ad adipiscendum bonum æternum, præmiumque cœleste speratum, videlicet propter consecutionem veræ felicitatis, quæ est expletio, id est actuatio, spei : ostentare, inquam, usque in finem vitæ præsentis. Qui enim perseveraverit usque in finem, salvus erit. Ut non segnes, id est pigri ac tepidi, efficiamini : prout in Apocalypsi cuidam improperatur, Habeo adversum te quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti ; et in eodem libro, Utinam frigidus esses aut calidus ; verum, id est sed, imitatores eorum efficiamini, qui fide et patientia, id est merito seu actibus fidei atque patientiæ, hereditabunt promissiones, id est, promissa cœlestia hereditarie possidebunt, quæ nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec cor capere valet.
paras.en: [[6:11|And we desire|Cupimus autem]], kindled with zeal for your salvation, [[6:11|that every one of you shew forth the same carefulness|unumquemque vestrum eamdem ostentare sollicitudinem]], that is, often to show the careful ministering mentioned before, [[6:11|to the accomplishing of hope|ad expletionem spei]], that is, for obtaining the eternal good and the hoped-for heavenly reward, namely for the attaining of true happiness, which is the fulfilment, that is, the actualizing, of hope: to show it, I say, [[6:11|unto the end|usque in finem]] of the present life. For [[Matt 24:13|he that shall persevere to the end, he shall be saved|Qui enim perseveraverit usque in finem, salvus erit]]. [[6:12|That you become not slothful|ut non segnes efficiamini]], that is, sluggish and lukewarm: as in the Apocalypse one is reproached, [[Apoc 2:4|I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first charity|Habeo adversum te quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti]]; and in the same book, [[Apoc 3:15|I would thou wert cold or hot|Utinam frigidus esses aut calidus]]; [[6:12|but|verum]], that is, rather, become [[6:12|followers of them|imitatores eorum]], [[6:12|who through faith and patience|qui fide et patientia]], that is, by the merit or acts of faith and patience, [[6:12|shall inherit the promises|hereditabunt promissiones]], that is, shall possess by inheritance the heavenly things promised, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart|nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec cor capere valet]] can contain.

paras.t: Quod autem factæ sint hominibus promissiones divinæ, consequenter ostenditur. Abrahæ namque promittens Deus bona terrena atque cœlestia, scilicet possessionem terræ Chanaan dandam semini suo, et omnes gentes benedicendas esse in semine suo, videlicet benedictione salutis æternæ, quoniam neminem, id est nullum, habuit per quem juraret, majorem : nil enim majus seu dignius est Deo, per quod possit Deus jurare ; juravit per semetipsum, dicens : Nisi benedicens benedicam te, id est, in spiritualibus ac temporalibus bonis copiam tibi præstabo : quod si non fecero, non mihi credatur, nec æstimer Deus ; et multiplicans multiplicabo te, id est, multos ex te filios procreabo. De hoc legitur in Genesi, quemadmodum Deus juraverit Abrahæ, quod semen ejus esset sicut stellæ cœli, et sicut arena maris. Et sic Abraham longanimiter ferens, id est diu patienter exspectans, adeptus est repromissionem, id est bona promissa, videlicet vitam æternam, et reliqua jam expressa.
paras.en: That divine promises were made to men is shown next. [[6:13|For God making promises to Abraham|Abrahæ namque promittens Deus]] goods earthly and heavenly, namely possession of the land of Chanaan to be given to his seed, and that all nations should be blessed in his seed, that is, with the blessing of eternal salvation[[Gen 12:1||]][[Gen 15:7||]][[Gen 15:18||]], [[6:13|because he had no one greater by whom he might swear|quoniam neminem habuit, per quem juraret, majorem]] (no one, that is, none): for nothing is greater or worthier than God, by which God could swear; [[6:13|swore by himself|juravit per semetipsum]], [[6:14|Saying: Unless blessing I shall bless thee|dicens : Nisi benedicens benedicam te]], that is, I shall give thee abundance of goods spiritual and temporal: and if I do not, let me not be believed nor reckoned God [Denis explains the Hebraic oath-formula “unless…” as an implied self-curse]; [[6:14|and multiplying I shall multiply thee|et multiplicans multiplicabo te]], that is, I shall beget many children from thee. Of this we read in Genesis, how God swore to Abraham that his seed should be as the stars of heaven and as the sand of the sea[[Gen 22:16||]][[Gen 22:17||]]. [[6:15|And so patiently enduring|Et sic Abraham longanimiter ferens]] Abraham, that is, waiting patiently a long time, [[6:15|he obtained the promise|adeptus est repromissionem]], that is, the promised goods, namely eternal life and the rest already mentioned.

paras.t: Cur autem Deus juravit, subjungitur, scilicet ad condescendendum infirmitati humanæ. Homines enim per majorem sui, id est per aliquem vere vel opinative digniorem, jurant. Confirmatio namque non fit nisi per aliquid certius atque stabilius. Idololatræ vero jurant per idola, quibus ipsi digniores sunt. Ipsi tamen idola sua deos esse putantes, arbitrantur se idolis inferiores. Et omnis controversiæ eorum finis, id est terminatio totius altercationis hominum, est juramentum, valens ad confirmationem ejus quod dicitur, cui aliter non crederetur, nisi juramento firmaretur. In quo, id est per quod juramentum Abrahæ factum, abundantius volens Deus ostendere pollicitationis suæ heredibus, id est electis divinas promissiones æternaliter possessuris, videlicet Abrahæ et semini ejus, immobilitatem consilii sui, id est invariabile propositum sapientiæ suæ, seu consilium suum immobile de salvandis. Consilium enim Dei immobile est ; et quamvis Deus mutet sententiam, non tamen consilium. Dum ergo consilium Dei juramento firmatur, multum abundanter ostenditur hominibus immobilitas divini consilii. Ideo subditur : interposuit jusjurandum, id est, sermoni quem habuit ad Abraham, miscuit juramentum, ut per duas res immobiles, id est per immobilitatem divini consilii, et infallibilitatem divini juramenti, quibus impossibile est mentiri Deum, qui est prima totius veritatis mensura, et veritas ipsa, fortissimum solatium, id est jucundam atque præcipuam securitatem sive fiduciam, habeamus de adeptione promissorum bonorum, qui confugimus ad Deum (dicentes : Domine, refugium factus es nobis), ad tenendam propositam spem, id est ad firmiter conservandam futuræ beatitudinis exspectationem.
paras.en: Why God swore is added next, namely to condescend to human weakness. [[6:16|For men swear by one greater than themselves|Homines enim per majorem sui jurant]], that is, by someone truly or reputedly worthier. For confirmation is made only by something more certain and stable. Idolaters, indeed, swear by idols, than which they themselves are worthier; yet they, thinking their idols gods, deem themselves inferior to them. [[6:16|and an oath for confirmation is the end of all their controversy|et omnis controversiæ eorum finis, ad confirmationem, est juramentum]], that is, the termination of every dispute among men, avails [[6:16|for confirmation|ad confirmationem]] of what is said, which otherwise would not be believed unless confirmed by oath. [[6:17|Wherein|In quo]], that is, by which oath made to Abraham, [[6:17|God, meaning more abundantly to shew to the heirs of the promise|abundantius volens Deus ostendere pollicitationis suæ heredibus]] (Denis reads “of *his* promise”), that is, to the elect who are to possess the divine promises eternally, namely Abraham and his seed, [[6:17|the immutability of his counsel|immobilitatem consilii sui]], that is, the unchangeable purpose of His wisdom, or His immovable counsel concerning those to be saved. For the counsel of God is immovable[[Is 46:10||]]; and although God changes His sentence, yet not His counsel. When therefore God's counsel is confirmed by oath, the immovability of the divine counsel is shown to men very abundantly. Hence it is added: [[6:17|interposed an oath|interposuit jusjurandum]], that is, He mingled an oath with the word He spoke to Abraham, [[6:18|That by two immutable things|ut per duas res immobiles]], that is, by the immovability of the divine counsel and the infallibility of the divine oath, [[6:18|in which it is impossible for God to lie|quibus impossibile est mentiri Deum]], who is the first measure of all truth and Truth itself, [[6:18|we may have the strongest comfort|fortissimum solatium habeamus]], that is, a joyful and special security or confidence about obtaining the promised goods, [[6:18|we who have fled for refuge|qui confugimus]] to God (saying: Lord, thou hast been our refuge[[Ps 89:1||]] [the margin seems to read Ps. lxxxix, 1, where the words stand]), [[6:18|to hold fast the hope set before us|ad tenendam propositam spem]], that is, to keep firmly the expectation of future beatitude.

paras.t: Quam spem sicut ancoram habemus animæ tutam ac firmam : id est, quemadmodum ancora corporalis tenet navim in fluctibus fixam, ne mergatur aut defluat, sic spes est spiritualis ancora animæ tuta et firma, id est secura et fortis, quoniam tenet animam inter prospera et adversa in Domino fixam atque illæsam. Unde in libro Machabæorum habetur : Omnes qui sperant in Domino, non infirmantur : et in Psalmo, Sperent in te qui noverunt nomen tuum, quoniam non dereliquisti quærentes te, Domine. Et incedentem, id est tendentem et nos introducentem, usque ad interiora velaminis, id est usque ad patriam Beatorum, quam modo non cernimus nisi fide, de cujus ratione est quædam obscuritas seu veritatis velamen. Interiora ergo velaminis, sunt secreta cœlestia seu beatitudo futura jam nobis velata. Inter Ecclesiam quippe militantem ac triumphantem interpositum est velamen. Ubi, id est quæ secreta patriæ, præcursor pro nobis, id est ad nostram utilitatem, introivit in ascensione, videlicet Jesus, qui exsultavit ut gigas ad currendam viam, et ante nos festinavit ad patriam, secundum ordinem Melchisedech pontifex factus in æternum. Hæc verba jam dicta sunt atque exposita.
paras.en: [[6:19|Which we have as an anchor of the soul, sure and firm|Quam spem sicut ancoram habemus animæ tutam ac firmam]]: that is, as a bodily anchor holds a ship fixed amid the waves, lest it sink or drift, so hope is the spiritual anchor of the soul, sure and firm, that is, secure and strong, since it holds the soul fixed and unharmed in the Lord amid prosperity and adversity. Hence in the book of Machabees we have: [[1 Mach 2:61|all generations: that none that trust in him, fail in strength|Omnes qui sperant in Domino, non infirmantur]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 9:11|And let them trust in thee who know thy name: for thou hast not forsaken them that seek thee|Sperent in te qui noverunt nomen tuum, quoniam non dereliquisti quærentes te, Domine]]. [[6:19|and which entereth in|Et incedentem]], that is, tending and leading us in, [[6:19|even within the veil|usque ad interiora velaminis]], that is, to the fatherland of the Blessed, which now we discern only by faith, to whose nature belongs a certain obscurity or veil of truth. The things within the veil, then, are the heavenly secrets, or the future beatitude now veiled from us. For between the Church militant and triumphant a veil is set. [[6:20|Where|Ubi]], that is, into which secrets of the fatherland, [[6:20|the forerunner Jesus is entered for us|præcursor pro nobis]], that is, for our profit, [[6:20|is entered|introivit]] at the Ascension, namely [[6:20|Jesus|Jesus]], who [[Ps 18:6|Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way|exsultavit ut gigas ad currendam viam]], and hastened before us to the fatherland, [[6:20|according to the order of Melchisedech|secundum ordinem Melchisedech pontifex factus in æternum]][[Ps 109:4||]]. These words have already been spoken and expounded.

11.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI UNDECIMI : EST AUTEM FIDES SPERANDARUM SUBSTANTIA RERUM, ARGUMENTUM NON APPARENTIUM.
11.title_en: Exposition of the eleventh chapter: Now faith is the substance of things to be hoped for, the evidence of things that appear not.

paras.t: Quoniam in fine præcedentis capituli dixit Apostolus, spiritualem vitam justi dependere ex fide tanquam ex fundamento; idcirco jam pandit præconia fidei, primo eam definiens, deinde efficaciam ejus per diversa exempla exponens. Sic ergo eam definit : Est autem fides sperandarum substantia rerum, id est habitus de rebus sperandis, videlicet de bonis futuris in patria, argumentum, id est adhæsio, non apparentium, id est supernaturalium veritatum, quæ per rationem comprehendi nequeunt vel videri. Sumitur itaque hoc loco substantia, non prout condistinguitur accidenti, sed pro quacumque entitate ; et argumentum accipitur pro effectu argumenti, scilicet pro adhæsione. Fides ergo vocatur substantia rerum sperandarum, id est prima inchoatio per quam res sperandæ nobis insunt. Apostolus vero non ponit definitionem fidei in propria forma, sed sic rediguntur verba ejus in definitionem fidei : Fides est habitus intellectus, quo inchoatur vita æterna in nobis, per quem consentit ratio non apparentibus seu supernaturalibus veritatibus. Cui definitioni concordat descriptio fidei quam capitulo 7 de Divinis nominibus Dionysius tradit, dicendo : Fides est manens credentium fundamentum, collocans eos in veritate, et veritatem in ipsis. Augustinus quoque : Fides, inquit, est virtus qua creduntur quæ non videntur. Et Damascenus : Fides est non inquisitus consensus.
paras.en: Since at the end of the preceding chapter the Apostle said that the spiritual life of the just man depends on faith as on its foundation, he now sets forth the praises of faith: first defining it, then showing its power through various examples. So he defines it thus: [[11:1|Now, faith is the substance of things to be hoped for|Est autem fides sperandarum substantia rerum]], that is, a habit concerning things to be hoped for, namely the future goods in the fatherland; [[11:1|the evidence|argumentum]], that is, the adhesion, [[11:1|of things that appear not|non apparentium]], that is, of supernatural truths, which cannot be grasped or seen by reason. Here, then, *substance* is taken not as it is distinguished from accident, but for any entity whatever; and *evidence* [Latin *argumentum*, literally “proof” or “argument”] is taken for the effect of an argument, namely adhesion. Faith is therefore called the substance of things to be hoped for, that is, the first beginning through which the things hoped for are present in us. The Apostle does not give the definition of faith in its proper form; but his words are reduced to a definition of faith thus: Faith is a habit of the intellect, by which eternal life is begun in us, through which reason assents to truths that do not appear, that is, supernatural truths. With this definition agrees the description of faith that Dionysius gives in the seventh chapter of *On the Divine Names*, saying: Faith is the abiding foundation of believers, setting them in the truth and the truth in them. Augustine too says: Faith is the virtue by which things not seen are believed. And Damascene: Faith is an assent without inquiry.

paras.t: Denique, quod fides sit substantia, id est inchoatio per quam insunt nobis speranda, id est beatitudo æterna, et ea per quæ ad eam pertingimus, quæ jam in nobis sunt per quamdam inchoationem, declarat Apostolus. In hac enim fide formata, quæ est virtus theologica, id est per fidem, vel potius per interiorem et exteriorem actum ejus, testimonium, id est attestationem justitiæ a Deo, consecuti sunt senes, id est patres antiqui. Perhibuit namque eis testimonium Deus, quod justi essent propter fidem ipsorum.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle shows that faith is a substance, that is, a beginning through which the things to be hoped for are present in us: eternal beatitude, and the things by which we reach it, which are already in us by a certain beginning. [[11:2|For by this|In hac enim]] formed faith [that is, faith quickened by charity], which is a theological virtue (that is, through faith, or rather through its interior and exterior act), [[11:2|the ancients|senes]], that is, the fathers of old, [[11:2|obtained a testimony|testimonium consecuti sunt]], that is, an attestation of justice from God. For God bore them witness that they were just because of their faith.

paras.t:
Fide, quæ est supernaturale lumen mentis, intelligimus aptata, id est ordinate producta ac sapienter disposita, esse sæcula, id est entia universi, verbo Dei, id est per Filium, de quo dicitur : Omnia per ipsum facta sunt. Vel, Verbo Dei, id est divino præcepto, juxta illud : Ipse mandavit, et creata sunt. Ut ex invisibilibus, id est informibus elementis : unde in Genesi, ubi habemus, Terra erat inanis et vacua, translatio qua utitur Origenes sic habet : Terra erat invisibilis; visibilia, id est mixta vel ipsa elementa formata et visu perceptibilia, fierent ex invisibilibus, id est, post creationem spiritualium substantiarum visibilia fierent, non posterioritate temporis, sed dignitatis. Vel, Ex invisibilibus, id est æternis ideis in mente divina splendentibus, quasi ex formis exemplaribus, visibilia fierent. Omnia enim condidit Deus secundum ideas seu exemplares suæ sapientiæ rationes, quemadmodum ait Boetius :
O qui perpetua mundum ratione gubernas.
Et post pauca :
Tu cuncta superno
Ducis ab exemplo, pulchrum pulcherrimus ipse
Mundum mente gerens, similique in imagine formans
Perfectasque jubens perfectum absolvere partes.
paras.en:
[[11:3|By faith|Fide]], which is a supernatural light of the mind, [[11:3|we understand that the world was framed|intelligimus aptata]], that is, produced in order and wisely disposed, [[11:3|the world|esse sæcula]], that is, the beings of the universe, [[11:3|by the word of God|verbo Dei]], that is, by the Son, of whom it is said: [[John 1:3|All things were made by him|Omnia per ipsum facta sunt]]. Or, *By the word of God*, that is, by the divine command, according to that saying: [[Ps 32:9|he commanded, and they were created|Ipse mandavit, et creata sunt]]. [[11:3|that from invisible things|Ut ex invisibilibus]], that is, from formless elements; hence in Genesis, where we have, [[Gen 1:2|the earth was void and empty|Terra erat inanis et vacua]], the translation Origen uses reads: The earth was invisible; [[11:3|visible things|visibilia]], that is, mixed bodies or the elements themselves once formed and perceptible to sight, [[11:3|might be made|fierent]] from invisible things. That is, after the creation of the spiritual substances, visible things were made, later not in time but in dignity. Or, *From invisible things*, that is, from the eternal ideas shining in the divine mind, as from exemplar forms, visible things might be made. For God made all things according to the ideas, the exemplar reasons of his wisdom, as Boethius says:
O thou who governest the world by everlasting reason.
And shortly after:
Thou drawest all things from the pattern above;
thyself most fair, bearing a fair world in thy mind,
and forming it in a like image,
bidding the perfect whole complete its perfect parts.

paras.t: Fide, id est ex fide divinæ providentiæ ac remunerationis futuræ, plurimam, id est pretiosiorem, hostiam Abel quam Cain frater ejus obtulit Deo. Obtulit enim Cain de fructibus terræ, Abel vero de primogenitis gregis sui et de adipibus eorum. Per quam fidem seu plurimam hostiam, testimonium consecutus est a Deo esse justus, id est, Deus testatus est eum esse justum. Ideo subditur : testimonium perhibente muneribus ejus Deo. Testimonium nempe perhibuit Deus muneribus seu hostiis Abel, quod sibi accepta essent, tam verbo quam facto : verbo, quum dixit per Moysen, Respexit Deus ad Abel et ad munera ejus; facto, quoniam ignis de cœlo descendens super hostiam, eam consumpsit. Unde translatio Theodotionis sic habet : Inflammavit Dominus super Abel et super munera ejus. Et per illam fidem atque fidelem oblationem, defunctus, id est a fratre occisus, adhuc loquitur, id est, merito suæ justitiæ justam vindictam exquirit de innocenti sua occisione, prout Dominus aiebat ad Cain : Vox sanguinis fratris tui clamat ad me de terra. Vel, Defunctus adhuc loquitur, id est, loquendi materiam nobis ministrat. Nam fides et opus ejus reddunt eum tam commendabilem ac imitabilem, ut semper commemoranda sint nobis, nec deficiat laus ejus de ore hominum usque in ævum.
paras.en: [[11:4|By faith|Fide]], that is, from faith in divine providence and future reward, [[11:4|Abel offered to God a sacrifice exceeding that of Cain|plurimam hostiam Abel, quam Cain, obtulit Deo]]: a sacrifice *exceeding*, that is, more precious, than Cain his brother offered. For Cain offered of the fruits of the earth[[Gen 4:3||]], but Abel [[Gen 4:4|of the firstlings of his flock, and of their fat|de primogenitis gregis sui et de adipibus eorum]]. [[11:4|by which|Per quam]] faith, or exceeding sacrifice, [[11:4|he obtained a testimony that he was just|testimonium consecutus est a Deo esse justus]] from God; that is, God testified that he was just. Therefore it is added: [[11:4|God giving testimony to his gifts|testimonium perhibente muneribus ejus Deo]]. For God bore witness to Abel's gifts or sacrifices that they were acceptable to him, both by word and by deed. By word, when he said through Moses: [[Gen 4:4|the Lord had respect to Abel, and to his offerings|Respexit Deus ad Abel et ad munera ejus]]. By deed, since fire coming down from heaven upon the sacrifice consumed it; hence the translation of Theodotion reads: The Lord kindled fire upon Abel and upon his gifts. [[11:4|And by it|Et per illam]] faith and faithful offering, [[11:4|he being dead|defunctus]], that is, slain by his brother[[Gen 4:8||]], [[11:4|yet speaketh|adhuc loquitur]]: that is, by the merit of his justice he demands just vengeance for his innocent slaying, as the Lord said to Cain: [[Gen 4:10|the voice of thy brother's blood crieth to me from the earth|Vox sanguinis fratris tui clamat ad me de terra]]. Or, *Being dead he yet speaketh*, that is, he furnishes us with matter for speech. For his faith and his work make him so praiseworthy and so worthy of imitation that they are ever to be recalled by us, and his praise shall not depart out of the mouth of men for ever[[Jdt 13:25||]].

paras.t: Fide, id est merito fidei, Enoch translatus est in paradisum terrestrem angelico obsequio, ne videret, id est, ne experiretur, mortem naturalem et corporalem in se ipso. Tamen in fine mundi morietur, sicut Elias : occidentur enim ab Antichristo. Vel, Ne videret mortem aliorum, præsertim tempore diluvii, quam videre miserabile erat. Et non inveniebatur ab hominibus eum quærentibus, quia transtulit illum Deus in paradisum terrestrem. Hoc est quod legitur in Genesi : Enoch ambulavit cum Deo, et non apparuit, quia transtulit illum Dominus. Ante translationem enim testimonium habuit placuisse Deo, quoniam Deus testabatur ad aliquos quod Enoch sibi placeret, et multi justi testimonium perhibebant justitiæ ejus antequam transferretur in paradisum. De hoc Enoch scriptum est per Sapientem : Placens Deo factus est dilectus, et vivens inter peccatores translatus est ; raptus est, ne malitia mutaret intellectum ejus.
paras.en: [[11:5|By faith|Fide]], that is, by the merit of faith, [[11:5|Henoch was translated|Enoch translatus est]] into the earthly paradise by the ministry of angels[[Gen 5:24||]], [[11:5|that he should not see death|Ne videret mortem]]: that is, that he should not experience natural and bodily death in himself. Yet at the end of the world he will die, as will Elias, for they will be slain by Antichrist. Or, *that he should not see* the death of others, especially at the time of the flood, which was a wretched thing to see. [[11:5|and he was not found|Et non inveniebatur]] by the men who sought him, [[11:5|because God had translated him|quia transtulit illum Deus]] into the earthly paradise. This is what is read in Genesis: [[Gen 5:24|he walked with God, and was seen no more: because God took him|ambulavit cum Deo, et non apparuit, quia transtulit illum Dominus]]. [[11:5|For before his translation he had testimony that he pleased God|Ante translationem enim testimonium habuit placuisse Deo]], since God testified to some that Enoch pleased him, and many just men bore witness to his justice before he was translated into paradise. Of this Enoch it is written by the Wise Man: [[Wis 4:10|He pleased God, and was beloved, and living among sinners, he was translated|Placens Deo factus est dilectus, et vivens inter peccatores translatus est]]; [[Wis 4:11|He was taken away, lest wickedness should alter his understanding|raptus est, ne malitia mutaret intellectum ejus]].

paras.t: Sine fide autem impossibile est placere Deo. Oportet namque habere habitum fidei et interiorem actum ejus, ad hoc ut opus sit meritorium, quoniam fides dirigit intellectum ad finem supernaturalem. Unde Romanis dixit Apostolus : Quidquid non est ex fide, peccatum est. Credere enim oportet accedentem ad Deum, id est colentem seu exorantem ipsum Deum, quia est, id est, quod Deus vere sit, puta quod sit unus verus Deus, cui maxime convenit esse. Hoc tamen per naturalem rationem cognosci potest, et multis philosophis ex proprii ingenii studio patuit. Nihilo minus credendum proponitur, quia communitas hominum cui providet Deus, non vacat hujusmodi naturalibus considerationibus de Deo. Credere quoque oportet, quod et inquirentibus se remunerator sit, id est, quod Deus cultoribus suis mercedem impendat. Sine horum duorum fide nemo adultus unquam salvari potuit. Nec sufficit fides ista, sed alia multa credere est necesse. Forsitan tamen suffecit ante legem scriptam, et item sub lege, quantum ad gentiles, quibus sola lex naturalis data erat, nec obligabantur ad legem Mosaicam, dummodo implicitam habuerint fidem de adventu incarnationeque Christi. Qui enim credit quod Deus remunerator est, credit providentiam Dei, et per consequens credit modum humanæ salvationis, saltem implicite. Nunquam vero potuit aliquis salvari ex puris naturalibus, quum et fides sit supernaturale donum, et gratia Dei vita æterna.
paras.en: [[11:6|But without faith it is impossible to please God|Sine fide autem impossibile est placere Deo]]. For one must have the habit of faith and its interior act for a work to be meritorious, since faith directs the intellect to a supernatural end. Hence the Apostle said to the Romans: [[Rom 14:23|all that is not of faith is sin|Quidquid non est ex fide, peccatum est]] [the margin gives Rom. xi, 23; the words are Rom 14:23]. [[11:6|For he that cometh to God must believe|Credere enim oportet accedentem ad Deum]], that is, one who worships or prays to God himself, [[11:6|that he is|quia est]]: that is, that God truly is, namely that he is the one true God, to whom being belongs most fully. This, however, can be known by natural reason, and was plain to many philosophers through the labour of their own minds. Nevertheless it is put forward to be believed, because the generality of men, for whom God provides, has no leisure for such natural reasonings about God. One must also believe [[11:6|and is a rewarder to them that seek him|et inquirentibus se remunerator sit]]: that is, that God bestows a reward on those who worship him. Without faith in these two things no adult could ever be saved. Nor does this faith suffice; many other things must be believed. Perhaps, however, it sufficed before the written law, and likewise under the law in the case of the gentiles, to whom only the natural law had been given and who were not bound to the Mosaic law, provided they had implicit faith in the coming and incarnation of Christ. For whoever believes that God is a rewarder believes in God's providence, and consequently believes, at least implicitly, in the manner of man's salvation. But no one could ever be saved by purely natural powers, since faith is a supernatural gift, and [[Rom 6:23|the grace of God, life everlasting|gratia Dei vita æterna]] [the margin gives Ibid. xi, 23; the words are Rom 6:23].

paras.t: Fide Noe responso accepto divinitus de his quæ adhuc non videbantur, id est de futuro diluvio et hominum generali interitu : de quibus ei oranti pro hominum emendatione, Deus respondit, Finis universæ carnis venit coram me, etc. ; metuens aptavit, id est, convenienter fecit et distinxit, arcam de lignis lævigatis pro receptione animalium, in salutem domus suæ, id est ad præservandum se ipsum et filios suos, suamque ac filiorum uxores a morte diluvii, per quam arcam seu fidem, damnavit mundum, id est, homines mundanos ostendit damnabiles, qui sibi arcam fabricanti credere noluerunt de futuro diluvio, neque pœnitentiam agere, sicut et Petrus in sua testatur epistola : Qui increduli fuerunt aliquando, sicut in diebus Noe quum fabricaretur arca ; et justitiæ quæ per fidem est, id est, quæ ex fide procedit, heres, id est perpetuus possessor seu patrum suorum dignus successor, est institutus per gratiam Dei. Ceteris enim pereuntibus, in eo et domo sua dumtaxat fides permansit.
paras.en: [[11:7|By faith Noe, having received an answer|Fide Noe responso accepto]] from God [[11:7|concerning those things which as yet were not seen|de his quæ adhuc non videbantur]], that is, concerning the coming flood and the general destruction of men[[Gen 6:1||]] [the margin gives Gen. vi, 1 and following; the answer quoted is Gen 6:13]. When he prayed for the amendment of men, God answered him concerning these things: [[Gen 6:13|The end of all flesh is come before me|Finis universæ carnis venit coram me]], etc. [[11:7|moved with fear, framed|metuens aptavit]], that is, fittingly made and divided, [[11:7|the ark|arcam]] of planed timber to receive the animals, [[11:7|for the saving of his house|in salutem domus suæ]], that is, to preserve himself and his sons, and his own wife and his sons' wives, from death by the flood; [[11:7|by the which he condemned the world|per quam damnavit mundum]]: by the which ark, or faith, he condemned the world, that is, he showed worldly men to be deserving of damnation, who would not believe him about the coming flood while he built the ark, nor do penance, as Peter also testifies in his epistle: [[1 Pet 3:20|Which had been some time incredulous, when they waited for the patience of God in the days of Noe, when the ark was a building|Qui increduli fuerunt aliquando, sicut in diebus Noe quum fabricaretur arca]]; [[11:7|and was instituted heir of the justice which is by faith|et justitiæ, quæ per fidem est, hæres est institutus]] by the grace of God: of the justice which is by faith, that is, which proceeds from faith, he was made heir, that is, its lasting possessor, or the worthy successor of his fathers. For when the rest perished, faith remained only in him and his house.

paras.t: Insuper ponit Apostolus exempla de patribus Judæorum, ostendens quod per fidem justificati sunt. Fide, qui vocatur Abraham, quod interpretatur pater multarum gentium, qui ante vocatus est Abram, id est pater excelsus, obedivit Deo jubenti : Egredere de terra tua et de cognatione tua. Obedivit ergo in locum exire, videlicet in terram Chanaan, quem accepturus erat a Deo in hereditatem : non utique in se, nec pro se, sed pro semine suo longo post tempore. Ait enim Stephanus in Actibus : Non dedit Dominus ei in ea hereditatem, nec passum pedis. Et exiit de terra propria, nesciens quo iret, donec Deus ei viam et terram monstravit. Unde fuerat quasi vagabundus.
paras.en: Next the Apostle gives examples from the fathers of the Jews, showing that they were justified by faith. [[11:8|By faith he that is called Abraham|Fide, qui vocatur Abraham]], which is interpreted *father of many nations*, who before was called Abram, that is, *high father*[[Gen 17:5||]], [[11:8|obeyed|obedivit]] God, who commanded: [[Gen 12:1|Go forth out of thy country, and from thy kindred|Egredere de terra tua et de cognatione tua]]. So he obeyed [[11:8|to go out into a place|in locum exire]], namely into the land of Chanaan, [[11:8|which he was to receive for an inheritance|quem accepturus erat a Deo in hereditatem]] from God: not indeed in his own person nor for himself, but for his seed long afterwards. For Stephen says in the Acts: [[Acts 7:5|And he gave him no inheritance in it: no, not the pace of a foot|Non dedit Dominus ei in ea hereditatem, nec passum pedis]]. [[11:8|And he went out|Et exiit]] from his own land, [[11:8|not knowing whither he went|nesciens quo iret]], until God showed him the way and the land. So he had been like a wanderer.

paras.t: Fide demoratus est in terra repromissionis, tanquam in aliena, quia in ea hereditatem non habuit ; in casulis, id est parvis tabernaculis seu tentoriis de loco ad locum portabilibus, habitando cum Isaac et Jacob coheredibus repromissionis ejusdem, quibus promissa est terra hæc, sicut et Abrahæ. Dicit Glossa hoc loco, quod non eodem tempore inhabitaverunt in terra hac. Verumtamen si littera Genesis diligentius attendatur, invenimus Abraham vixisse post nativitatem Jacob : quod etiam Lyra satis declarat. Idcirco dimitto. Eodem ergo tempore habitaverunt in terra præfata, ut alii dicunt. Ideo vero morari non horruit in terra aliena : Expectabat enim fundamenta habentem civitatem, id est, firmiter speravit tandem ingredi cœlestem patriam in æternum fundatam, seu immobiliter stabilitam, cujus artifex et conditor est Deus, non homo.
paras.en: [[11:9|By faith he abode in the land of promise, as in a strange country|Fide demoratus est in terra repromissionis, tanquam in aliena]], because he had no inheritance in it; [[11:9|dwelling in cottages|in casulis habitando]], that is, in little tabernacles or tents that could be carried from place to place, [[11:9|with Isaac and Jacob, the co-heirs of the same promise|cum Isaac et Jacob coheredibus repromissionis ejusdem]], to whom this land was promised as it was to Abraham. The Gloss says on this place that they did not dwell in this land at the same time. But if the letter of Genesis is studied more carefully, we find that Abraham lived on after the birth of Jacob, as Lyra also shows clearly enough. Therefore I set the Gloss aside: they dwelt in that land at the same time, as others say. And he did not shrink from staying in a strange land, [[11:10|For he looked for a city that hath foundations|Expectabat enim fundamenta habentem civitatem]]: that is, he firmly hoped at last to enter the heavenly fatherland, founded for ever, or established immovably, [[11:10|whose builder and maker is God|cujus artifex et conditor est Deus]], not man.

paras.t: Fide, id est merito fidei Abrahæ, vel propria fide, et ipsa Sara sterilis per naturam, virtutem, id est fecunditatem, in conceptionem seminis, id est ad concipiendum ex semine viri, accepit, etiam præter tempus ætatis, quoniam nonagenaria erat, desierantque ei fieri muliebria, quoniam fidelem, id est in promissis veracem, credidit esse eum qui repromiserat quod Isaac nasceretur ex Sara. Dicunt quidam, hoc non posse exponi de Sara, quia ex infidelitate risit, propter quod angelus eam redarguit, sed de Abraham, qui licet riserit, non tamen ex dubitatione, sed admiratione et gaudio. Alii vero exponunt de Sara, dicentes eam post increpationem iteratæ promissioni angeli credidisse.
paras.en: [[11:11|By faith|Fide]], that is, by the merit of Abraham's faith, or by her own faith, [[11:11|also Sara herself, being barren|et ipsa Sara sterilis]] by nature, [[11:11|received strength to conceive seed|virtutem in conceptionem seminis accepit]]: strength, that is, fruitfulness, *to conceive seed*, that is, to conceive from the seed of her husband; [[11:11|even past the time of age|etiam præter tempus ætatis]], since she was ninety years old and it had ceased to be with her after the manner of women[[Gen 17:17||]][[Gen 18:11||]]; [[11:11|because she believed that he was faithful who had promised|quoniam fidelem credidit esse eum qui repromiserat]]: she believed him *faithful*, that is, true to his promises, who had promised that Isaac would be born of Sara. Some say this cannot be explained of Sara, because she laughed from unbelief and the angel rebuked her for it[[Gen 18:12||]], but must be explained of Abraham, who, though he laughed, did so not from doubt but from wonder and joy[[Gen 17:17||]]. Others explain it of Sara, saying that after the rebuke she believed the angel's repeated promise.

paras.t: Propter quod, id est propter hanc fidem Abrahæ vel Saræ, et ab uno patriarcha Abraham orti sunt Judæi, et hoc emortuo, id est ab ipso Abraham vetustate confecto, ac infecundo quantum ad Saram seu quamlibet vetulam. Unde ad Romanos dictum est, quod non consideravit corpus suum emortuum. Postmodum tamen plurimos generavit filios de Cetura femina juniore. Senex namque de juvencula generare potest. Vel, Ab uno, utero Saræ, et hoc emortuo, id est naturali calore destituto. Orti ergo sunt de uno filii, tanquam sidera cœli in multitudinem, et sicut arena quæ est ad oram, id est ad littus, maris, innumerabilis. Propter multitudinem enim comparati sunt stellis cœli et arenæ maris, secundum quod Dominus locutus est Abrahæ : Suspice cœlum, et numera stellas, si potes ; sic erit semen tuum. Quoniam tamen in populo isto ex Abraham et Sara nato, fuerunt quidam electi, et alii reprobi, per stellas intelligi possunt electi, per arenam innumerabilem reprobi.
paras.en: [[11:12|For which cause|Propter quod]], that is, because of this faith of Abraham or of Sara, [[11:12|there sprung even from one|et ab uno patriarcha Abraham orti sunt]], the patriarch Abraham, the Jews, [[11:12|and him as good as dead|et hoc emortuo]]: that is, from Abraham himself, worn out with age and unfruitful as regards Sara or any old woman. Hence it is said in Romans that he considered not his own body now dead[[Rom 4:19||]]. Yet afterwards he begot many sons of Cetura, a younger woman[[Gen 25:1||]], for an old man can beget of a young girl. Or, *from one*, the womb of Sara, *and that as good as dead*, that is, bereft of natural heat. So sons sprang from one, [[11:12|as the stars of heaven in multitude and as the sand which is by the sea shore innumerable|tanquam sidera cœli in multitudinem, et sicut arena quæ est ad oram, id est ad littus, maris, innumerabilis]]: *by the sea shore*, that is, on the coast of the sea. For on account of their multitude they are compared to the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea, as the Lord spoke to Abraham: [[Gen 15:5|Look up to heaven and number the stars if thou canst. And he said to him: So shall thy seed be|Suspice cœlum, et numera stellas, si potes ; sic erit semen tuum]]. But since in this people born of Abraham and Sara some were elect and others reprobate, the stars can be taken for the elect and the innumerable sand for the reprobate.

paras.t: Juxta fidem, id est in fide, seu fidei adhærendo, defuncti sunt omnes isti qui post diluvium fuerunt, vel omnes præter Enoch translatum, non acceptis repromissionibus, id est non adeptis cœlestibus bonis eis promissis, sed a longe, id est de terra et valle hac lacrimarum, seu fidei obscuritate, eas adspicientes oculo fidei : contemplabantur enim promissa cœlestia ; et salutantes, id est affectuose ad eas suspirantes seu hilariter eis applaudentes, quemadmodum nautæ civitatem ad quam navigant intuentes, salutant eamdem ; et confitentes quia peregrini et hospites sunt super terram. Hic enim quasi in exsilio habitaverunt, juxta illud in Psalmo : Ne sileas, quoniam advena ego sum apud te et peregrinus, sicut omnes patres mei.
paras.en: [[11:13|All these died according to faith|Juxta fidem defuncti sunt omnes isti]]: *according to faith*, that is, in faith, or cleaving to faith; *all these* who lived after the flood, or all except Enoch, who was translated; [[11:13|not having received the promises|non acceptis repromissionibus]], that is, not having obtained the heavenly goods promised them, [[11:13|but beholding them afar off|sed a longe eas adspicientes]]: *afar off*, that is, from the earth and this vale of tears, or in the obscurity of faith, beholding them with the eye of faith, for they contemplated the heavenly promises; [[11:13|and saluting them|et salutantes]], that is, sighing for them with longing, or joyfully hailing them, as sailors who catch sight of the city they are sailing to salute it; [[11:13|and confessing that they are pilgrims and strangers on the earth|et confitentes quia peregrini et hospites sunt super terram]]. For they lived here as in exile, according to that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 38:13|Be no silent: for I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner as all my fathers were|Ne sileas, quoniam advena ego sum apud te et peregrinus, sicut omnes patres mei]].

paras.t: Qui enim hæc dicunt, id est, qui se in hac vita hospites et peregrinos esse veraciter asserunt, significant, id est, verbo et facto ostendunt, se patriam inquirere, non terrenam, sed cœlestem, sicut subjungitur : Et si quidem illius patriæ meminissent [de qua exierunt], id est, si Chaldææ ac Mesopotamiæ recordati fuissent cum affectu redeundi, habebant utique tempus revertendi ad patriam illam. Nunc autem meliorem appetunt, id est, modo sic est, quod suo tempore meliorem patriam optaverunt, id est cœlestem, respectu cujus peregrinos se esse professi sunt. Jacob tamen rediit in Mesopotamiam, sed non ad perseverandum in ea. Ideo non confunditur, id est, indignum vel indecens non arbitratur, Deus omnipotens, qui est omnium Deus, vocari Deus eorum specialiter, eo quod ei specialiter adhæreant, eumque honorent in omnibus, et ipse singulariter provideat eis. Propter quod Dominus ait ad Moysen : Hæc dices filiis Israel : Deus patrum vestrorum, Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob, misit me ad vos : hoc nomen mihi est in æternum, et hoc est memoriale meum in generationem et generationem. [Paravit enim illis civitatem.]
paras.en: [[11:14|For they that say these things|Qui enim hæc dicunt]], that is, who truly declare themselves strangers and pilgrims in this life, [[11:14|do signify|significant]], that is, show by word and deed, [[11:14|that they seek a country|se patriam inquirere]], not an earthly but a heavenly one, as is added: [[11:15|And truly, if they had been mindful of that from whence they came out|Et si quidem illius patriæ meminissent [de qua exierunt]], that is, if they had remembered Chaldea and Mesopotamia with a desire to go back, [[11:15|they had doubtless, time to return|habebant utique tempus revertendi]] to that country. [[11:16|But now they desire a better|Nunc autem meliorem appetunt]]: that is, as it is, in their own time they longed for a better country, [[11:16|that is to say, a heavenly country|id est cœlestem]], in respect of which they professed themselves pilgrims. Jacob did return to Mesopotamia, but not to remain there[[Gen 28:5||]][[Gen 31:18||]]. [[11:16|Therefore, God is not ashamed|Ideo non confunditur Deus]]: that is, Almighty God, who is the God of all, does not think it unworthy or unbecoming [[11:16|to be called their God|vocari Deus eorum]] in a special way, because they cleave to him in a special way and honour him in all things, and he provides for them singularly. For this reason the Lord said to Moses: [[Ex 3:15|Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: The Lord God of your fathers the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob hath sent me to you; this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations|Hæc dices filiis Israel : Deus patrum vestrorum, Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob, misit me ad vos : hoc nomen mihi est in æternum, et hoc est memoriale meum in generationem et generationem]]. [[11:16|for he hath prepared for them a city|Paravit enim illis civitatem]] [these words are printed in brackets in the edition].

paras.t: Fide obtulit, id est, offerre paratus fuit, Abraham Isaac filium suum, quum tentaretur ipse Abraham a Deo : qui tentat, non ut fallat aut sciat, sed ut occasionem promerendi ministret, et alios scire quid faciat ; et unigenitum offerebat. Non quod solum Isaac pro tunc habebat in filium : habuit namque et alios multos de Cetura ; sed solus Isaac fuit heres, et natus de libera. Qui Abraham susceperat repromissiones, id est iteratas promissiones implendas per Isaac, scilicet, quod multos filios procrearet, et terram Chanaan possideret in semine Isaac :
paras.en: [[11:17|By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered Isaac|Fide obtulit Abraham Isaac]]: *offered*, that is, was ready to offer, Isaac his son[[Gen 22:1||]], [[11:17|when he was tried|quum tentaretur]], Abraham himself, by God, who tempts not to deceive or to find out, but to furnish an occasion of merit and to let others know what one will do; [[11:17|offered up his only begotten son|et unigenitum offerebat]]. Not that Isaac was then his only son, for he had many others by Cetura[[Gen 25:1||]]; but Isaac alone was the heir and born of the free woman[[Gen 21:10||]][[Gen 21:12||]][[Gal 4:30||]]. [[11:17|and he that had received the promises|Qui Abraham susceperat repromissiones]], Abraham, that is, the repeated promises to be fulfilled through Isaac: that he would beget many sons and would possess the land of Chanaan in the seed of Isaac;

paras.t: ad quem Abraham dictum est a Deo : Quia in Isaac vocabitur tibi semen, id est, nati ex Isaac, vocabuntur filii tui, et bona tibi promissa consequentur. Huic autem promissioni repugnare videbatur oblatio Isaac, qui tempore illo nondum genuit prolem ; sed Abraham non dubitavit de veritate promissionis divinæ. Cujus ratio subditur : arbitrans, scilicet Abraham, quia et a mortuis suscitare potens est Deus, non solum Isaac filium suum, sed omnem defunctum. Non enim videbatur alius modus quo posset impleri divina promissio de multiplicatione filiorum ab Isaac, si Isaac oblatus fuisset, nisi resuscitaretur. Et quoniam Abraham scivit Deum hoc posse, non dubitavit in fide. Unde et Abraham eum, videlicet Isaac, in parabolam, id est typicam significationem, accepit. Intellexit namque per Isaac significari Christum, et per immolationem Isaac, Christi passionem. Per hoc tamen quod non Isaac, sed aries immolatus est, præfigurabatur quod Christus secundum divinitatem suam impassibilis fuit, secundum humanitatem vero occisus est.
paras.en: [[11:18|To whom it was said|ad quem Abraham dictum est]], to Abraham, by God: [[11:18|In Isaac shalt thy seed be called|Quia in Isaac vocabitur tibi semen]][[Gen 21:12||]][[Rom 9:7||]]: that is, those born of Isaac shall be called thy sons and shall obtain the goods promised thee. Now the offering of Isaac seemed to contradict this promise, since at that time he had not yet begotten offspring; but Abraham did not doubt the truth of the divine promise. The reason is added: [[11:19|Accounting|arbitrans]], Abraham, that is, [[11:19|that God is able to raise up even from the dead|quia et a mortuis suscitare potens est Deus]], not only Isaac his son but every dead man[[1 Kings 2:6||]]. For there seemed no other way in which the divine promise of the multiplying of sons from Isaac could be fulfilled, if Isaac had been offered, unless he were raised again. And since Abraham knew that God could do this, he did not waver in faith. [[11:19|Whereupon also he received him for a parable|Unde et … eum … in parabolam … accepit]]: Abraham received him, namely Isaac, *for a parable*, that is, as a type. For he understood that Christ was signified by Isaac, and Christ's passion by the sacrifice of Isaac. But by the fact that not Isaac but a ram was sacrificed, it was prefigured that Christ was impassible according to his divinity, but was slain according to his humanity.

paras.t: Fide et de futuris, id est de futurorum bonorum collatione, benedixit Isaac patriarcha Jacob et Esau filiis suis. Benedictio namque eorum fuit de bonis futuris, quia impleta non fuit in illis duobus filiis Isaac : non enim Esau servivit Jacob. Sed impleta fuit in populis natis ex illis. Nam tempore David et Salomonis Idumæi orti ex Esau, servierunt Judæis filiis Jacob. Per hoc autem quod Jacob ante Esau benedictionem sortitus est, mystice signabatur quod populus christianus junior consequeretur benedictionem Judæorum.
paras.en: [[11:20|By faith also of things to come|Fide et de futuris]], that is, concerning the bestowing of future goods, [[11:20|Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau|benedixit Isaac patriarcha Jacob et Esau]][[Gen 27:27||]][[Gen 27:39||]], the patriarch blessed his sons. For their blessing concerned future goods, since it was not fulfilled in those two sons of Isaac: Esau did not serve Jacob. It was fulfilled in the peoples born of them, for in the time of David and Solomon the Idumæans, sprung from Esau, served the Jews, the sons of Jacob[[2 Kings 8:14||]] [the margin gives II Reg. xiii, 14; the subjection of Edom is told at 2 Kings 8:14]. And by Jacob's obtaining the blessing before Esau it was mystically signified that the younger, Christian people would obtain the blessing of the Jews.

paras.t: Fide Jacob moriens, id est morti propinquans, singulos filiorum Joseph benedixit, videlicet Ephraim et Manassen, præponens Ephraim juniorem Manassæ seniori : quoniam Deo revelante prævidit regnum decem tribuum transferendum ad filios Ephraim, quod in Jeroboam cœpit impleri ; et quoniam novit tribum Ephraim majorem futuram. Et adoravit fastigium virgæ ejus, id est, ipse Jacob post benedictionem filiorum Joseph, et juramentum quo Joseph juravit quod sepeliret patrem suum in terra Chanaan in spelunca duplici, tunc ipse Jacob adoravit Deum, innixus, erectus vel incumbens super fastigium, id est cacumen, virgæ ejus, id est baculi sui, quem propter senectutem tenebat in manibus ; vel, Virgæ ejus, id est sceptri quod Joseph portavit in signum traditæ sibi potestatis super Ægyptum, quod Jacob accepit in manibus suis quando Joseph juravit. Quo juramento completo, Jacob innitens sceptri fastigio adoravit, conversus ad caput lectuli, ut nostra habet translatio. Loco cujus translatio Septuaginta interpretum continet, Adoravit fastigium virgæ ejus, sicut hic allegatur.
paras.en: [[11:21|By faith Jacob, dying|Fide Jacob moriens]], that is, drawing near to death, [[11:21|blessed each of the sons of Joseph|singulos filiorum Joseph benedixit]][[Gen 48:1||]], namely Ephraim and Manasses, putting Ephraim the younger before Manasses the elder, because by God's revelation he foresaw that the kingdom of the ten tribes would pass to the sons of Ephraim, which began to be fulfilled in Jeroboam[[3 Kings 11:26||]][[3 Kings 12:20||]], and because he knew that the tribe of Ephraim would be the greater. [[11:21|and adored the top of his rod|Et adoravit fastigium virgæ ejus]]: that is, after the blessing of Joseph's sons, and after the oath by which Joseph swore that he would bury his father in the land of Chanaan in the double cave[[Gen 47:29||]], Jacob adored God, leaning, upright or resting, upon the top, that is, the head, *of his rod*, that is, of his staff, which he held in his hands because of old age. Or, *of his rod*, that is, of the sceptre which Joseph bore as a sign of the power given him over Egypt, which Jacob took into his hands when Joseph swore. When the oath was done, Jacob, leaning on the top of the sceptre, adored, turning to the bed's head, as our translation has it[[Gen 47:31||]]. In its place the translation of the Seventy reads, *He adored the top of his rod*, as it is quoted here.

paras.t: Fide Joseph moriens, de profectione filiorum Israel memoratus est, id est, egressum eorum ex Ægypto prædixit ; et de ossibus suis mandavit, id est, filiis Israel præcepit ut tollerent secum ossa sua, sepelirentque ea in spelunca duplici, secundum quod dicitur, in qua sepulti sunt Adam et Eva, Abraham et Sara, Isaac, Jacob et Lia. Unde dixit Joseph : Deus visitabit vos, efferte ossa mea vobiscum. In hac quippe terra sepeliri volebant sancti Patriarchæ, secundum Hieronymum, quia noverant in ea Christum nasciturum atque passurum, ut simul cum eo resurgerent, cum quo scimus multorum Sanctorum qui dormierant, corpora resurrexisse.
paras.en: [[11:22|By faith Joseph, when he was dying, made mention of the going out of the children of Israel|Fide Joseph moriens, de profectione filiorum Israel memoratus est]], that is, he foretold their going out of Egypt[[Gen 50:23||]]; [[11:22|and gave commandment concerning his bones|et de ossibus suis mandavit]], that is, he charged the children of Israel to take his bones with them and to bury them in the double cave, in which, as is said, Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sara, Isaac, Jacob and Lia were buried[[Gen 50:24||]]. Hence Joseph said: [[Gen 50:24|God will visit you, carry my bones with you|Deus visitabit vos, efferte ossa mea vobiscum]] [the margin gives Gen. l, 23, 24; by Vulgate numbering the words are at 50:24]. For the holy Patriarchs wished to be buried in this land, according to Jerome, because they knew that Christ would be born and would suffer in it, so that they might rise together with him, with whom, we know, the bodies of many of the Saints that had slept arose[[Matt 27:52||]].

paras.t: Fide Moyses natus, occultatus est mensibus tribus a parentibus suis, ex fide parentum. Diutius autem eum celare non poterant. Occultaverunt vero eum, eo quod vidissent elegantem infantem, id est præter solitum venustate et gratia magis decoratum : propter quod speraverunt Deum aliquid magni operaturum per illum infantem ; et non timuerunt timore completo, quamvis aliqualiter timuerint, regis edictum, id est Pharaonis præceptum, qui jussit omnes masculos Hebræorum necari, et in flumen jactari.
paras.en: [[11:23|By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents|Fide Moyses natus, occultatus est mensibus tribus a parentibus suis]][[Ex 2:2||]], by the faith of his parents. They could not hide him longer[[Ex 2:3||]]. They hid him [[11:23|because they saw he was a comely babe|eo quod vidissent elegantem infantem]], that is, adorned beyond the usual with beauty and grace, for which reason they hoped God would work something great through that child; [[11:23|and they feared not|et non timuerunt]] with full fear, though they feared somewhat, [[11:23|the king's edict|regis edictum]], that is, the command of Pharao, who ordered all the male children of the Hebrews to be killed and cast into the river[[Ex 1:22||]].

paras.t: Fide Moyses grandis factus mente et corpore, id est virtuosus atque adultus, negavit operibus, quamvis non verbis, videlicet occidendo Ægyptium et fugiendo regis palatium, se esse filium adoptivum filiæ Pharaonis, quæ eum adoptavit in filium ; magis eligens affligi cum populo Dei, id est cum filiis Israel, qui tunc vehementer ab Ægyptiis opprimebantur, quam temporalis peccati habere jucunditatem, id est, quam esse in regis palatio, atque corporalibus transitoriisque frui deliciis ; majores divitias æstimans thesauro Ægyptiorum, improperium Christi, id est, persecutionem et tribulationem figurativam passionis Christi, utiliorem et fructuosiorem judicans universis Ægypti deliciis. Adspiciebat enim in remunerationem, id est, justum Dei judicium et universorum debitam retributionem pensavit, quam scilicet momentaneum et leve tribulationis præsentis, æternum gloriæ pondus operetur in nobis. Unde Psalmista : Inclinavi, inquit, cor meum ad faciendas justificationes tuas in æternum, propter retributionem. Verumtamen magis convertendus est oculus mentis ad Dei honorem, quam ad propriam mercedem ; potiusque induci debemus ad bene agendum ac patiendum ex divino amore, quam remunerationis desiderio : aliter essemus mercenarii, non servi fideles neque amici.
paras.en: [[11:24|By faith Moses, when he was grown up|Fide Moyses grandis factus]] in mind and body, that is, virtuous and adult, [[11:24|denied|negavit]] by deeds, though not by words (namely by killing the Egyptian and fleeing the king's palace[[Ex 2:11||]]), [[11:24|himself to be the son of Pharao's daughter|se esse filium adoptivum filiæ Pharaonis]]: her adopted son, for she adopted him as her son[[Ex 2:10||]]; [[11:25|Rather choosing to be afflicted with the people of God|magis eligens affligi cum populo Dei]], that is, with the children of Israel, who were then being grievously oppressed by the Egyptians, [[11:25|than to have the pleasure of sin for a time|quam temporalis peccati habere jucunditatem]], that is, than to be in the king's palace and enjoy bodily and passing delights; [[11:26|Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasure of the Egyptians|majores divitias æstimans thesauro Ægyptiorum, improperium Christi]]: *the reproach of Christ*, that is, the persecution and tribulation that prefigured Christ's passion, judging it more profitable and fruitful than all the delights of Egypt. [[11:26|For he looked unto the reward|Adspiciebat enim in remunerationem]]: that is, he weighed God's just judgment and the due retribution of all, how, namely, [[2 Cor 4:17|that which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation worketh for us above measure, exceedingly an eternal weight of glory|momentaneum et leve tribulationis præsentis, æternum gloriæ pondus operetur in nobis]]. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:112|I have inclined my heart to do thy justifications for ever, for the reward|Inclinavi … cor meum … propter retributionem]]. Yet the eye of the mind should be turned more to God's honour than to one's own reward, and we ought to be moved to do and suffer well by divine love rather than by desire of reward; otherwise we would be hirelings, not faithful servants nor friends.

paras.t: Fide reliquit Ægyptum, non veritus animositatem regis, id est superbiam Pharaonis. Hoc quidam intelligunt de fuga Moysis ab Ægypto statim percusso Ægyptio. Unde Chrysostomus dicit : Quod Moyses primo fugit in terram Madian, non fuit metus, sed fides, quia credebat se liberari a Deo. Noluit in Ægypto manere, ne esset causa jactantiæ si se in apertum præcipitaret periculum. Verumtamen in Exodo manifeste habetur, quod Moyses timuit quum audisset patefactum esse homicidium quo occidit Ægyptium, et fugit a facie Pharaonis. Ideo alii exponunt hæc de egressu Moysis ex Ægypto simul cum filiis Israel. Quibus obviare videtur quod subditur de celebratione Paschæ, quæ præcessit egressum prædictum : nisi dicatur, quod non servatur hoc loco ordo rei gestæ.
