Invisibilem enim Deum tanquam videns sustinuit, id est, tam fiducialiter exspectavit, et in ejus auxilio confidebat, ac si eum vidisset.
paras.en: [[11:27|By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the fierceness of the king|Fide reliquit Ægyptum, non veritus animositatem regis]]: *the fierceness*, that is, the pride, of Pharao. Some understand this of Moses' flight from Egypt immediately after he struck the Egyptian[[Ex 2:15||]] [the margin note here is mostly illegible]. Hence Chrysostom says: That Moses first fled into the land of Madian was not fear but faith, because he believed he would be delivered by God. He would not stay in Egypt, lest it be a cause of boasting if he threw himself into open danger. Yet in Exodus it is plainly stated that Moses feared when he heard that the homicide by which he killed the Egyptian had been discovered, and fled from the face of Pharao[[Ex 2:14||]]. Therefore others explain these words of Moses' going out of Egypt together with the children of Israel. Against them seems to stand what is added about the celebration of the Pasch, which came before that going out, unless it be said that the order of events is not kept in this place. [[11:27|for he endured, as seeing him that is invisible|Invisibilem enim Deum tanquam videns sustinuit]]: that is, he waited for God, the invisible, as confidently, and trusted in his help, as if he had seen him.

paras.t: Fide celebravit Moyses Pascha, id est agni paschalis immolationem, esum ac ritum, credens populum hoc modo salvandum ; et sanguinis agni illius effusionem celebravit, liniendo postes et superliminaria domorum sanguine agni, secundum imperium Domini ; ne qui vastabat primitiva, id est, ne angelus occidens primogenita hominum et jumentorum in tota Ægypto, tangeret eos, id est, Hebræos vastaret. Jusserat enim Dominus Moysi, ut filii Israel sanguine agni postes et superliminaria domorum suarum linirent, quatenus angelus cernens domos ita linitas, transiliret, nec tangeret habitatores. Quo figurabatur, quod signati sanguine Christi, non opprimuntur a tentatore.
paras.en: [[11:28|By faith he celebrated the pasch|Fide celebravit Moyses Pascha]], Moses: that is, the sacrifice, eating and rite of the paschal lamb[[Ex 12:1||]], believing that the people would be saved in this way; [[11:28|and the shedding of the blood|et sanguinis agni illius effusionem]] of that lamb he celebrated, smearing the posts and lintels of the houses with the lamb's blood at the Lord's command; [[11:28|that he who destroyed the firstborn might not touch them|ne qui vastabat primitiva, tangeret eos]]: that is, that the angel who slew the firstborn of men and beasts in all Egypt might not destroy the Hebrews. For the Lord had commanded Moses that the children of Israel should smear the posts and lintels of their houses with the lamb's blood, so that the angel, seeing the houses so marked, would pass over and not touch those who dwelt there. By this it was figured that those signed with the blood of Christ are not overcome by the tempter.

paras.t: Fide filii Israel transierunt mare Rubrum, id est per alveum exsiccatum, in quo paulo ante aqua maris fluebat, tanquam per aridam terram, aqua maris divina virtute divisa, et existente ea filiis Israel pro muro a dextris et a sinistris ; quod iter experti, id est attentantes, Ægyptii sequentes filios Israel per viam maris Rubri, demersi sunt, id est submersi in currentibus eis aquis, et Domino eos involvente in mediis fluctibus.
paras.en: [[11:29|By faith they passed through the Red Sea|Fide filii Israel transierunt mare Rubrum]], the children of Israel: that is, through the dried bed in which shortly before the water of the sea had flowed, [[11:29|as by dry land|tanquam per aridam terram]], the water of the sea having been divided by divine power and standing [[Ex 14:22|as a wall on their right hand and on their left|pro muro a dextris et a sinistris]] for the children of Israel; [[11:29|which the Egyptians attempting|quod … experti … Ægyptii]]: which path the Egyptians *attempting*, that is, venturing upon it as they followed the children of Israel by way of the Red Sea, [[11:29|were swallowed up|demersi sunt]], that is, drowned as the waters ran together upon them, the Lord shutting them up in the midst of the waves[[Ex 14:23||]][[Ex 14:27||]][[Ex 14:28||]].

paras.t: Fide, id est merito fidei Israelitarum credentium Deo, muri Jericho corruerunt miraculose, virtute divina, circuitu dierum septem, id est completo circuitu qui per septem dies factus est semel unoquoque die a toto populo Israel. Fide, id est propter fidem, Rahab meretrix non periit, id est, occisa non est, cum incredulis Chananæis, quoniam credidit Deum esse verum ac omnipotentem, ita ut daret filiis Israel terram Chanaan, sicut promisit, excipiens exploratores duos viros missos a Josue, cum pace. Nam occultavit eos, atque pacifice dimisit eosdem.
paras.en: [[11:30|By faith|Fide]], that is, by the merit of the faith of the Israelites who believed God, [[11:30|the walls of Jericho fell down|muri Jericho corruerunt]] miraculously, by divine power[[Jos 6:16||]][[Jos 6:20||]], [[11:30|by the going round them seven days|circuitu dierum septem]], that is, when the going round had been completed, made once each day for seven days by the whole people of Israel. [[11:31|By faith|Fide]], that is, because of faith, [[11:31|Rahab the harlot perished not with the unbelievers|Rahab meretrix non periit cum incredulis]][[Jos 6:25||]]: she was not slain with the unbelieving Chanaanites, because she believed that God is true and almighty, so that he would give the children of Israel the land of Chanaan as he had promised[[Jos 2:11||]], [[11:31|receiving the spies with peace|excipiens exploratores cum pace]]: the two men sent by Josue. For she hid them and let them go in peace[[Jos 2:6||]][[Jos 2:15||]].

paras.t: Et quid adhuc dicam ? id est, totum quod præsentem concernit materiam, explicare non possum. Deficiet enim me tempus enarrantem, id est, spatium vitæ vel conscriptionis hujus epistolæ mihi nimis breve erit ad eloquendum : de Gedeon, cui angelus dixit : Dominus tecum, virorum fortissime ; qui cum viris trecentis debellavit numerosissimum exercitum Madianitarum ; Barac filio Abinoem, qui cum decem millibus pugnatorum occidit centum millia adversariorum ; Samson, id est de Samsone filio Manue ex tribu Dan, qui Philistæos oppressit ; Jephthe Galaadite, qui filios Ammon dejecit ; David rege, qui adhuc adolescens, leonem, ursum, atque gigantem exstinxit ; Samuel filio Elcanæ, qui post Heli judicavit Israelem ; et aliis Prophetis veteris Testamenti. Ex his constat, quod omnes jam nominati, sancti fuerunt, quia in Sanctorum ponuntur catalogo. Unde si aliqua illicita commiserunt, pœnitentiam fecisse creduntur : ut Gedeon, de hoc quod contra legem fecit sibi ephod, seu vestem sacerdotalem ; et Jephthe, de hoc quod propriam obtulit filiam : nisi dicatur hoc fecisse ex occulto Spiritus Sancti instinctu. Ex quo motus est et Samson ad occidendum se ipsum cum hostibus suis. Ideo de sanctitate Samsonis dubitandum non est.
paras.en: [[11:32|And what shall I yet say?|Et quid adhuc dicam?]] That is, I cannot set out all that concerns the present matter. [[11:32|For the time would fail me to tell|Deficiet enim me tempus enarrantem]]: that is, the span of my life, or of the writing of this epistle, will be far too short for me to tell [[11:32|of Gedeon|de Gedeon]], to whom the angel said: [[Judg 6:12|The Lord is with thee, O most valiant of men|Dominus tecum, virorum fortissime]], who with three hundred men overthrew the vast army of the Madianites[[Judg 7:7||]]; of [[11:32|Barac|Barac]] the son of Abinoem, who with ten thousand fighting men slew a hundred thousand of the enemy[[Judg 4:6||]] [the margin gives Judic. ix, 6; Barac's story is in Judg 4]; of [[11:32|Samson|Samson]], that is, of Samson the son of Manue, of the tribe of Dan, who crushed the Philistines[[Judg 16:30||]]; of [[11:32|Jephthe|Jephthe]] the Galaadite, who overthrew the children of Ammon[[Judg 11:32||]]; of King [[11:32|David|David]], who while still a youth slew a lion, a bear and a giant[[1 Kings 17:35||]][[1 Kings 17:36||]][[1 Kings 17:49||]]; of [[11:32|Samuel|Samuel]] the son of Elcana, who judged Israel after Heli[[1 Kings 7:15||]]; [[11:32|and the prophets|et prophetis]], the other Prophets of the Old Testament. From this it is clear that all those named were holy, since they are set in the catalogue of the Saints. Hence, if they committed anything unlawful, they are believed to have done penance: as Gedeon, for having made himself an ephod, that is, a priestly garment, against the law[[Judg 8:27||]]; and Jephthe, for having offered his own daughter[[Judg 11:39||]], unless it be said that he did this by a secret prompting of the Holy Ghost. By such a prompting Samson too was moved to kill himself together with his enemies[[Judg 16:30||]]; and so there is no doubting the holiness of Samson.

paras.t: Qui jam præfati per fidem vicerunt regna Madian, Ammonitarum, Philistinorum, Syrorum, etc. Quæ omnia in libro Judicum plenius continentur. Operati sunt justitiam. Justus enim ex fide vivit, et prædicti judices justa exercuerunt judicia. Adepti sunt repromissiones, id est bona eis promissa. Aliqua enim promissa in præsenti sortiti sunt vita, puta victorias, principatum et pacem ; aliqua vero, post vitam hanc, maxime post Christi adventum, videlicet bona cœlestia. Quod autem supra dictum est, Juxta fidem hi omnes defuncti sunt, non acceptis promissionibus, intelligitur de promissionibus patriæ. Obturaverunt, id est, occidendo, vel a devoratione prohibendo, clauserunt, ora leonum, ut David, Samson et Daniel ; exstinxerunt impetum ignis, ut Aaron, et tres pueri in camino ; effugaverunt, id est, in fugam verterunt, aciem gladii, id est exercitum gladiis cinctum : sicut in libris Judicum, Regum et Paralipomenon sæpissime recitatur ; convaluerunt miraculose de infirmitate letali, ut Ezechias et Job ; fortes facti sunt in bello corporali contra hostes visibiles, et spirituali contra invisibiles, ut patet de David, et Machabæo et fratribus ejus ; castra verterunt, id est destruxerunt, exterorum, id est alienigenarum ; acceperunt mulieres, videlicet mulier Sunamitis et vidua Sidonia, de resurrectione, id est mediante resurrectione, seu per resuscitationem ex mortuis, mortuos suos, id est filios suos defunctos. Elias namque resuscitavit filium viduæ Sidoniæ, Eliseus filium mulieris Sunamitis.
paras.en: [[11:33|Who by faith conquered kingdoms|qui per fidem vicerunt regna]]: those already named conquered the kingdoms of Madian, of the Ammonites, the Philistines, the Syrians, etc., all of which is told more fully in the book of Judges. [[11:33|wrought justice|Operati sunt justitiam]]. For [[Hab 2:4|the just shall live in his faith|Justus enim ex fide vivit]][[Rom 1:17||]], and these judges executed just judgments. [[11:33|obtained promises|Adepti sunt repromissiones]], that is, the goods promised them. For some of the promises they obtained in this present life, such as victories, rule and peace; others after this life, chiefly after the coming of Christ, namely the heavenly goods. What was said above, [[11:13|All these died according to faith, not having received the promises|Juxta fidem … defuncti sunt … promissionibus]][[Heb 11:13||]], is understood of the promises of the fatherland. [[11:33|stopped the mouths of lions|obturaverunt ora leonum]]: *stopped*, that is, closed them, by killing them or by keeping them from devouring, as David, Samson and Daniel did[[1 Kings 17:35||]][[Judg 14:6||]][[Dan 6:22||]][[Dan 14:39||]]; [[11:34|Quenched the violence of fire|exstinxerunt impetum ignis]], as Aaron did, and the three children in the furnace[[Num 16:47||]][[Num 16:48||]][[Dan 3:50||]]; [[11:34|escaped the edge of the sword|effugaverunt, id est, in fugam verterunt, aciem gladii]]: Denis reads *effugaverunt*, that is, they put to flight the edge of the sword, that is, an army girt with swords [the Vulgate has *effugerunt*, “escaped”], as is told very often in the books of Judges, Kings and Paralipomenon; [[11:34|recovered strength from weakness|convaluerunt miraculose de infirmitate]] miraculously, from mortal sickness, as Ezechias and Job did[[4 Kings 20:7||]][[Job 42:10||]]; [[11:34|became valiant in battle|fortes facti sunt in bello]], in bodily battle against visible enemies and in spiritual battle against invisible ones, as is plain in David, and in Machabeus and his brothers; [[11:34|put to flight the armies of foreigners|castra verterunt exterorum]]: they overthrew, that is, destroyed, the camps of foreigners, that is, of aliens; [[11:35|Women received their dead raised to life again|acceperunt mulieres de resurrectione mortuos suos]]: namely the Sunamite woman and the widow of Sidon received *their dead*, that is, their dead sons, *by resurrection*, that is, through being raised from the dead. For Elias raised the son of the widow of Sidon, and Eliseus the son of the Sunamite woman[[3 Kings 17:22||]][[4 Kings 4:35||]].

paras.t: Alii autem Sanctorum pro fide distenti sunt, id est in tormentis extenti, ut legitur de septem fratribus Machabæis et aliis quibusdam, non suscipientes redemptionem, id est præsentium pœnarum evasionem, ut meliorem invenirent resurrectionem in die novissimo (quam inventuri non erant, si præsentes pœnas curassent evadere), id est, quatenus beatam immutationem atque felicem suscitationem in die judicii consequi mererentur. De qua secundo Machabæorum unus fratrum illorum dicebat : Rex mundi Deus, defunctos nos pro suis legibus in æternæ vitæ resurrectione suscitabit.
paras.en: [[11:35|But others were racked|alii autem distenti sunt]]: others of the Saints, for the faith, were stretched out in torments, as is read of the seven Machabee brothers and certain others[[2 Mach 7:1||]]; [[11:35|not accepting deliverance|non suscipientes redemptionem]], that is, escape from present pains, [[11:35|that they might find a better resurrection|ut meliorem invenirent resurrectionem]] on the last day (which they would not have found had they sought to escape the present pains); that is, so that they might deserve to obtain a blessed change and a happy raising up on the day of judgment. Of this one of those brothers said, in the second book of Machabees: [[2 Mach 7:9|the King of the world will raise us up, who die for his laws, in the resurrection of eternal life|Rex mundi Deus, defunctos nos pro suis legibus in æternæ vitæ resurrectione suscitabit]].

paras.t: Alii vero ludibria, id est irrisiones, contumeliasque verborum, et verbera experti, insuper et vincula et carceres, id est incarcerationes. In eo quod ait, Insuper, notat hæc in eisdem facta personis, videlicet in Jeremia, Samsone, Michæa. Lapidati sunt, ut Jeremias in Ægypto, Zacharias filius Joiadæ pontificis inter templum et altare ; secti sunt, ut Isaias a Manasse ; tentati sunt adversitatibus, ut Tobias, vel blandis promissionibus ut averterentur a Deo, ut Mathathias et Eleazarus ; in occisione gladii, id est gladio facta, mortui sunt : nam et Manasses implevit Jerusalem sanguine innocentium usque ad os. Circuierunt varia mundi loca in melotis, id est in vestibus factis de pilis camelorum, sicut Joannes Baptista. Vel, melota est pellis hispida animalis quod dicitur melus. In pellibus caprinis, ut Elias. Egentes victu atque amictu, angustiati, id est diversis animi afflictionibus pressi, afflicti in corpore.
paras.en: [[11:36|And others had trial of mockeries|Alii vero ludibria, et verbera experti]]: *mockeries*, that is, derision and insulting words, [[11:36|and stripes: moreover also of bands and prisons|et verbera experti, insuper et vincula et carceres]], that is, imprisonments. By saying *moreover*, he notes that these things were done to the same persons, namely to Jeremias, Samson and Michæas[[Jer 37:14||]][[Judg 16:21||]][[3 Kings 22:27||]]. [[11:37|They were stoned|Lapidati sunt]], as Jeremias in Egypt, and Zacharias, the son of Joiada the high priest, between the temple and the altar[[2 Par 24:20||]]; [[11:37|they were cut asunder|secti sunt]], as Isaias by Manasses; [[11:37|they were tempted|tentati sunt]] by adversities, as Tobias was[[Tob 2:1||]], or by flattering promises meant to turn them from God, as Mathathias and Eleazar were[[1 Mach 2:17||]][[1 Mach 2:18||]][[2 Mach 6:21||]][[2 Mach 6:22||]]; [[11:37|they were put to death by the sword|in occisione gladii mortui sunt]]: they died by slaughter done with the sword, for Manasses too filled Jerusalem with innocent blood up to the mouth[[4 Kings 21:16||]]. [[11:37|they wandered about in sheepskins|circuierunt in melotis]]: they went about various places of the world *in sheepskins* [Latin *melotis*], that is, in garments made of camel's hair, like John the Baptist[[Matt 3:4||]]. Or, a *melota* is the shaggy hide of an animal called the *melus* [the badger]. [[11:37|in goatskins|In pellibus caprinis]], as Elias did[[4 Kings 1:8||]]. [[11:37|being in want|Egentes]] of food and clothing, [[11:37|distressed|angustiati]], that is, pressed by various afflictions of mind, [[11:37|afflicted|afflicti]] in body.

paras.t: Quibus dignus non erat mundus, id est mundanorum hominum cœtus : quia et ipsi ea quæ mundi sunt vilipenderunt, et mundus propter suam impietatem dignus non fuit conversatione ipsorum. In solitudinibus, id est locis desertis, errantes per devia, ut David cum suis tempore Saulis, et Mathathias cum suis tempore Antiochi Illustris ; in montibus, et in speluncis, et in cavernis terræ commorantes, ut legitur de Elia et filiis Prophetarum, quos abscondit Abdias tempore Jezabel. Unde et David : Ecce, inquit, elongavi fugiens, et mansi in solitudine. Fugerunt enim hominum adspectus ac strepitus, ut Deo vacarent liberius.
paras.en: [[11:38|Of whom the world was not worthy|Quibus dignus non erat mundus]]: *the world*, that is, the company of worldly men; for they themselves held cheap the things of the world, and the world, because of its impiety, was not worthy of their company. [[11:38|wandering in deserts|in solitudinibus errantes]]: in deserted places, wandering by trackless ways, as David did with his men in the time of Saul[[1 Kings 23:14||]], and Mathathias with his in the time of Antiochus the Illustrious[[1 Mach 2:28||]][[2 Mach 5:27||]]; [[11:38|in mountains and in dens and in caves of the earth|in montibus, et in speluncis, et in cavernis terræ]] dwelling, as is read of Elias and of the sons of the Prophets whom Abdias hid in the time of Jezabel[[3 Kings 18:4||]][[3 Kings 19:9||]]. Hence David too says: [[Ps 54:8|Lo, I have gone far off flying away; and I abode in the wilderness|Ecce elongavi fugiens, et mansi in solitudine]]. For they fled the sight and the noise of men, so as to be free for God.

paras.t: Et hi omnes testimonio fidei, id est actione procedente ex fide, vel passione propter fidem suscepta, dante testimonium eis quod vere fideles fuerunt, probati, id est divinitus approbati, commendabilesque effecti, non acceperunt repromissionem, id est cœlestem hereditatem promissam, ante Christi passionem ; Deo pro nobis, id est pro nostra utilitate, melius aliquid providente, videlicet, ut non sine nobis consummarentur, id est, ne ante ministros novi testamenti æterna beatitudine perfruerentur. Detinebantur enim in limbo usque ad Christi passionem : ante quam decollatus est Joannes Baptista, novi testamenti minister et præco. Sicque propter majus gaudium procurandum simul beatificati sunt Sancti antiqui, et aliqui qui erant tempore Christi. Vel sic : Non acceperunt repromissionem, id est corporis stolam seu glorificationem, Deo pro nobis aliquid melius providente, ut non sine nobis consummarentur, id est, ne ante diem judicii hanc gloriam consequerentur, sed tunc omnes simul suscitemur et conglorificemur, atque de beatitudine tanta mutuo congratulemur.
paras.en: [[11:39|And all these, being approved by the testimony of faith|Et hi omnes testimonio fidei]]: that is, the action proceeding from faith, or the suffering undergone for faith, bearing them witness that they were truly faithful; [[11:39|being approved|probati]], that is, approved by God and made praiseworthy, [[11:39|received not the promise|non acceperunt repromissionem]], that is, the promised heavenly inheritance, before the passion of Christ; [[11:40|God providing some better thing for us|Deo pro nobis aliquid melius providente]]: *for us*, that is, for our benefit, providing something better, namely [[11:40|that they should not be perfected without us|ut non sine nobis consummarentur]]: that is, that they should not enjoy eternal beatitude before the ministers of the new testament. For they were held in limbo until the passion of Christ, before which John the Baptist, minister and herald of the new testament, was beheaded[[Matt 14:10||]]. So, to bring about a greater joy, the ancient Saints were beatified together with some who lived in the time of Christ. Or thus: *They received not the promise*, that is, the robe of the body, its glorification, God providing something better for us, that they should not be perfected without us: that is, that they should not obtain this glory before the day of judgment, but that then we should all be raised and glorified together, and rejoice with one another in so great a beatitude.
